senses.gloss: Bravely and with spirit, especially in a hard fight.
examples: The team fought *gallantly* but lost in overtime.
The firefighters worked *gallantly* through the night.

senses.gloss: Politely and attentively, especially in an old-fashioned way toward a woman.
examples: He *gallantly* offered her his coat.
The old man *gallantly* held the door for us.

senses.gloss: Bravely and willingly, especially when doing something hard or unpleasant.
examples: She *gamely* tried the spicy soup, then reached for water.
The injured runner *gamely* finished the race.
He smiled *gamely* through the whole awkward dinner.

position: before its word — before a participle (*garishly painted*); end after a verb

senses.gloss: In a way that is too bright, colorful, or showy.
examples: The casino was *garishly* lit with neon.
She wore a *garishly* patterned shirt to the funeral.
The motel rooms were decorated *garishly* in pink and gold.

position: before its word — before a participle (*gaudily painted*); end after a verb

senses.gloss: In a way that is too bright, showy, and cheap-looking.
examples: The trailer was *gaudily* painted in purple and orange.
Tourists crowded the *gaudily* lit shops along the boardwalk.
She dressed *gaudily*, with gold chains and bright scarves.

position: end — also before its word (*generically named*)

senses.gloss: As a whole class or type, not as a particular one.
examples: In some states, all soft drinks are *generically* called "coke."
The report refers to them *generically* as "contractors."

senses.gloss: Under a common, non-brand name, and usually more cheaply.
examples: The drug is now available *generically* at a much lower price.
Ask your pharmacist whether the medicine is sold *generically*.

senses.gloss: Freely and in large amounts; giving more than is needed or expected.
examples: Our neighbors donated *generously* to the school fundraiser.
Apply sunscreen *generously* before you go outside.
She has always treated her employees *generously*.

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle; front as a viewpoint adverb

senses.gloss: In terms of genes, or by changing genes.
examples: Most of the corn grown in the US is *genetically* modified.
Eye color is largely *genetically* determined.
*Genetically*, the two species are almost identical.

senses.gloss: In a friendly, cheerful, and pleasant way.
examples: The host greeted each guest *genially* at the door.
He chatted *genially* with reporters after the game.
"Come on in," she said *genially*.

senses.gloss: Softly and carefully, without force or roughness.
examples: She *gently* picked up the sleeping baby.
Stir the sauce *gently* so it doesn't break.
Could you tell him the news more *gently*?

senses.gloss: Gradually, not steeply or suddenly.
examples: The path slopes *gently* down to the lake.
Let the soup simmer *gently* for an hour.

position: before its word — before an adjective (*geologically active*); front as a viewpoint adverb

senses.gloss: In terms of geology, the study of rocks and the earth's structure.
examples: Yellowstone is one of the most *geologically* active places on earth.
*Geologically*, the Appalachians are much older than the Rockies.
The site is *geologically* unstable, so nobody can build there.

position: end — also before its word (*geometrically precise*)

senses.gloss: In terms of shapes, lines, and angles.
examples: The garden is laid out in *geometrically* perfect squares.
The two triangles are *geometrically* similar.

senses.gloss: By repeated multiplication, and so very fast.
examples: The number of cases grew *geometrically* in the first month.
Costs rise *geometrically* as the project gets bigger.

senses.gloss: In a silly, excited, or light-headed way.
examples: The kids laughed *giddily* on the roller coaster.
She was *giddily* happy after getting the job offer.
Fans ran *giddily* onto the field after the win.

form: not from *ginger* — an old word that is also an adjective (*a gingerly step*)

senses.gloss: Very carefully and slowly, so as not to cause pain or damage.
examples: He stepped *gingerly* onto the icy sidewalk.
She *gingerly* touched the bruise on her knee.
The committee approached the topic *gingerly*.

position: before its word — before *slow*; end after a verb

senses.gloss: Extremely slowly, like a moving glacier.
examples: Progress on the new highway has been *glacially* slow.
The line at the DMV moved *glacially*.

senses.gloss: In a cold, unfriendly way.
examples: She smiled *glacially* and said nothing.
"That won't be necessary," he replied *glacially*.

senses.gloss: Willingly and happily.
examples: I'd *gladly* help you move this weekend.
Most customers would *gladly* pay more for faster shipping.
She accepted the invitation *gladly*.

senses.gloss: Very clearly and noticeably, usually about something bad.
examples: The mistake in the headline was *glaringly* obvious.
The report leaves out one *glaringly* important fact.
His answer was *glaringly* incomplete.

senses.gloss: With great, excited delight, often at someone else's bad luck.
examples: The kids tore *gleefully* into their presents.
The tabloids *gleefully* reported every detail of the divorce.
"I told you so," she said *gleefully*.

senses.gloss: Too easily and smoothly, without real thought or sincerity.
examples: The salesman answered every question a little too *glibly*.
Politicians talk *glibly* about cutting waste.
You can't *glibly* dismiss a problem this serious.

ru: по всему миру, в мировом масштабе
position: end — also before its word (*globally known*)

senses.gloss: Around the whole world; worldwide.
senses.ru: по всему миру, в мировом масштабе
examples: The company now sells its products *globally*.
Think *globally*, act locally.
She is a *globally* recognized expert on climate.

senses.gloss: In a sad, hopeless, or depressed way.
examples: He stared *gloomily* out the window at the rain.
"We're never going to finish," she said *gloomily*.
Analysts *gloomily* predicted another bad quarter.

position: before its word — before an adjective; end after a verb

senses.gloss: Wonderfully; in a very beautiful or enjoyable way.
examples: It was a *gloriously* sunny day at the beach.
The old theater has been *gloriously* restored.
The dessert was *gloriously* messy.

senses.gloss: In a way that brings great fame, honor, or success.
examples: The team's season ended *gloriously* with a championship.
Her career began *gloriously* but ended in scandal.

senses.gloss: With great praise.
examples: She spoke *glowingly* of her old math teacher.
Critics wrote *glowingly* about the new musical.
His former boss described him *glowingly* in the reference letter.

senses.gloss: In a quiet, unhappy, disappointed way.
examples: The players sat *glumly* in the locker room after the loss.
"I guess we're not going," he said *glumly*.
She *glumly* looked at the pile of dishes.

contrast: Offensive to many people, especially religious ones, and much stronger than *damn* or *really* — avoid it at work, in class, and with strangers. Also spelled *goddam* and *goddamned*. The same word works as an adjective (*the goddamn car*) and an interjection; those uses belong elsewhere.

senses.gloss: Very; extremely — a strong, rude way to add force.
examples: You're *goddamn* right I'm angry.
It's *goddamn* cold out here.
That was a *goddamn* stupid thing to say.

type: manner — informal and nonstandard in writing
comparison: not gradable — standard English uses *better* and *best*, the forms of *well*
form: flat — the same form as the adjective *good*
contrast: The standard adverb is *well*: *She did well on the test*. Americans say *did good* all the time, but teachers and editors mark it wrong. After linking verbs *good* is an adjective and correct: *You look good*, *It smells good*. *I feel good* means happy; *I feel well* means healthy. *Do good* (help others) uses the noun.

senses.gloss: Well (informal, not accepted in careful speech or writing).
examples: He played real *good* last night.
The car runs *good* now that it's been fixed.
She did *good* on her driving test.

senses.gloss: Thoroughly; completely (informal).
examples: They beat us *good* in the final.
He got fooled *good* by that email.

senses.gloss: In a friendly, patient, easygoing way.
examples: He laughed *good-naturedly* at the joke about his accent.
The crowd waited *good-naturedly* in the rain.
She *good-naturedly* agreed to take the extra shift.

position: before its word — before a participle or adjective; end after a verb

senses.gloss: In a very beautiful or attractive way.
examples: The book is *gorgeously* illustrated.
The bride looked *gorgeously* elegant in white.
The movie is *gorgeously* shot, even if the story is thin.

senses.gloss: With smooth, elegant, attractive movement.
examples: The dancers moved *gracefully* across the stage.
A heron landed *gracefully* on the water.
She skates more *gracefully* than anyone on the team.

senses.gloss: Politely and with dignity, especially in a difficult situation.
examples: He accepted defeat *gracefully*.
Not everyone learns to age *gracefully*.

contrast: A false friend: *graciously* is not *грациозно* — that is *gracefully*. *Graciously* means kindly and politely, often of someone important who could have refused.

senses.gloss: In a kind, polite, and generous way.
examples: The governor *graciously* agreed to meet with the students.
Our hosts welcomed us *graciously* into their home.
She *graciously* thanked everyone who had helped.

senses.gloss: Slowly, a little at a time, over a period.
examples: The weather *gradually* got warmer.
*Gradually*, she began to trust him again.
Increase the dose *gradually* over two weeks.

position: before its word — before an adjective (*grammatically correct*); front or end otherwise

senses.gloss: In terms of grammar, or according to its rules.
examples: The sentence is *grammatically* correct but sounds strange.
*Grammatically*, the two languages are very different.
Try to write *grammatically*, even in text messages.

position: end — also before a participle (*grandly named*)

senses.gloss: In an impressive, splendid, or self-important way.
examples: The hotel lobby was *grandly* decorated with marble and gold.
He announced his plans *grandly*, but nothing happened.
The *grandly* named "Palace Diner" is a tiny room with six stools.

position: end — also before its word (*graphically violent*)

senses.gloss: In very clear, vivid, and often shocking detail.
examples: The book describes the battle *graphically*.
Some scenes are too *graphically* violent for children.
The accident showed *graphically* why seat belts matter.

senses.gloss: Using charts, pictures, or other visual means.
examples: The results are shown *graphically* on the next page.
Can you present the data *graphically*?

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you are thankful.
examples: She *gratefully* accepted the ride home.
All donations will be *gratefully* received.
He smiled *gratefully* at the nurse.

type: manner — formal or humorous; everyday speech says *for free*
form: from Latin 'as a favor'; also an adjective (*The drinks are gratis*)

senses.gloss: Without charge; for free.
examples: The lawyer agreed to handle the case *gratis*.
Copies of the report are available *gratis* to members.
He fixed our computer *gratis*, just to be nice.

position: before its word — before an adjective (*gratuitously violent*); end after a verb
contrast: In modern English it almost never means *бесплатно*, even though *gratis* and *gratuity* (a tip) look related. It means 'for no good reason', and it is always a criticism.

senses.gloss: Without any good reason; more than is needed or acceptable.
examples: The movie is *gratuitously* violent.
He was *gratuitously* rude to the waiter.
Why insult them so *gratuitously*?

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle (*gravely ill*); end after a verb

senses.gloss: Very seriously, in a way that is dangerous or worrying.
examples: Her father is *gravely* ill.
We are *gravely* concerned about the safety of the workers.
The police *gravely* underestimated the size of the crowd.

senses.gloss: In a serious, solemn manner.
examples: The doctor nodded *gravely* and closed the file.
"This is a serious matter," the judge said *gravely*.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows a strong wish for more food, money, or things.
examples: The kids ate the cookies *greedily*.
He *greedily* grabbed the biggest piece.
The dog drank *greedily* from the bowl.

position: before its word — before a participle (*grievously wounded*); mid with verbs

senses.gloss: Very seriously, causing great harm or suffering.
examples: The soldier was *grievously* wounded in the attack.
The company *grievously* underestimated the cost of the cleanup.
These families have been *grievously* wronged.

position: end — also mid or before its word (*grimly determined*)

senses.gloss: In a very serious, stern, or gloomy way.
examples: "We'll have to start over," he said *grimly*.
Rescue workers searched *grimly* through the rubble.
She was *grimly* determined to finish the race.

contrast: Informal *gross* means 'disgusting', but *grossly* does not: it means 'extremely', always about something wrong or unfair (*grossly overpaid*, *grossly unfair*).

senses.gloss: Extremely; to a very bad or unacceptable degree.
examples: The story was *grossly* exaggerated.
Many of these workers are *grossly* underpaid.
It would be *grossly* unfair to punish the whole class.

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle; end after a verb

senses.gloss: In a strange, ugly, or absurdly exaggerated way.
examples: His face was *grotesquely* swollen after the fight.
The executives were paid *grotesquely* large bonuses.
The statue's hands are *grotesquely* oversized.

senses.gloss: Unwillingly, because you have to and not because you want to.
examples: He *grudgingly* admitted that she was right.
The landlord *grudgingly* agreed to fix the heater.
She shook his hand *grudgingly*.

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle; end after a verb

senses.gloss: In a horrible way, especially involving death or injury.
examples: The victims had been *gruesomely* murdered.
The documentary is *gruesomely* detailed about the surgery.
The horror movie ends *gruesomely*.

senses.gloss: In a rough, low, unfriendly-sounding voice.
examples: "Sit down," the coach said *gruffly*.
The old man answered *gruffly*, but he was smiling.
He *gruffly* told the reporters to leave.

senses.gloss: In a bad-tempered, easily annoyed way.
examples: "It's too early," he muttered *grumpily*.
She *grumpily* got out of bed.
The cat stared at us *grumpily* from the couch.

position: before its word — before an adjective (*guardedly optimistic*); end after a verb

senses.gloss: Carefully, without showing too much feeling or giving too much information.
examples: Doctors are *guardedly* optimistic about her recovery.
The spokesman answered questions *guardedly*.
She spoke *guardedly* about her time in prison.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you feel you have done something wrong.
examples: The boy looked *guiltily* at the broken vase.
She *guiltily* hid the candy wrapper.
He smiled *guiltily* when we caught him.

senses.gloss: Regularly, as a habit, usually over a long time.
examples: He is *habitually* late for meetings.
People who *habitually* skip breakfast often snack more.
The bill targets drivers who *habitually* speed.

modifies: adjectives, participles, and verbs (*I half expected*)
contrast: Before an adjective, participle or verb *half* is an adverb (*half empty*, *half done*); before a noun it is a determiner or noun (*half an hour*, *half the class*) and belongs elsewhere. Russian *полу-* is joined to the word (*полусонный*), but English writes *half* as a separate word after a verb (*I was half asleep*) and usually hyphenates it before a noun (*a half-eaten sandwich*).

senses.gloss: To the extent of fifty percent; partly, not completely.
examples: I was *half* asleep when you called.
The work is only *half* done.
I *half* expected him to say no.

senses.gloss: Without real effort, interest, or enthusiasm.
examples: He *half-heartedly* apologized and left.
The kids cleaned their rooms *half-heartedly*.
She waved *half-heartedly* from the car.

modifies: verbs of buying, selling, and getting in
form: compound of *half* + *price*; also an adjective (*half-price tickets*)
contrast: The same idea is often said *at half price* or *half off* (*Everything is half off*). Before a noun, *half-price* is an adjective.

senses.gloss: For half the usual cost.
examples: Kids under twelve get in *half-price*.
I bought the jacket *half-price* at the end-of-season sale.
On Tuesdays you can see a movie *half-price*.

senses.gloss: Slowly and with many pauses, because of uncertainty or difficulty.
examples: He spoke *haltingly* in his new language.
The little girl read the sentence *haltingly*.
Talks between the two sides moved forward *haltingly*.

position: end — also before a participle (*handily located*)
contrast: The 'easily, by a wide margin' sense is chiefly American (*won handily*); British English uses *handily* mainly for 'conveniently'.

senses.gloss: Easily and by a wide margin.
senses.ru: легко, без труда, с большим отрывом
examples: The senator won reelection *handily*.
Our team *handily* beat last year's champions.

senses.gloss: Conveniently; in a useful place or way.
examples: The hotel is *handily* located near the airport.
The charger fits *handily* into your pocket.

position: end — also before a participle (*handsomely dressed*)

senses.gloss: Generously; in a large amount.
examples: The consultants were paid *handsomely* for their advice.
Her early investment in the company paid off *handsomely*.
The volunteers were *handsomely* rewarded.

senses.gloss: In an attractive, elegant, well-made way.
examples: The room was *handsomely* furnished in dark wood.
The book is *handsomely* bound in leather.

position: end — also before a participle (*haphazardly arranged*)

senses.gloss: Without any plan, order, or care.
examples: Books were stacked *haphazardly* on the floor.
The rules seem to be enforced *haphazardly*.
He threw his clothes *haphazardly* into a suitcase.

type: manner; also viewpoint (*Happily, no one was hurt*)
position: mid or end — front in the 'fortunately' sense
modifies: verbs, adjectives (*happily married*), and whole clauses

senses.gloss: In a happy, contented way.
examples: The kids played *happily* in the backyard.
They've been *happily* married for thirty years.
The dog wagged its tail *happily*.

senses.gloss: Willingly; with pleasure.
examples: I'd *happily* drive you to the airport.
She would *happily* work weekends for more money.

senses.gloss: Fortunately; used to comment on a whole situation.
examples: *Happily*, no one was hurt in the fire.
The surgery went well, *happily*.

senses.gloss: Without causing any damage or injury.
examples: The rocket fell *harmlessly* into the ocean.
The storm passed *harmlessly* to the north of the city.
The ball bounced *harmlessly* off his helmet.

senses.gloss: Peacefully and in agreement, or in a pleasing combination.
examples: The two families lived *harmoniously* side by side.
The new building blends *harmoniously* with the old town.
Can the teams work together *harmoniously*?

senses.gloss: Severely, cruelly, or too strictly.
examples: The critics judged the film too *harshly*.
Prisoners there were treated *harshly*.
Her boss spoke to her more *harshly* than he needed to.

senses.gloss: In a way that is unpleasantly rough or strong to the senses.
examples: The office was *harshly* lit with fluorescent tubes.
The old gate creaked *harshly* in the wind.

senses.gloss: Very quickly, often too quickly to be careful.
examples: He *hastily* wrote a note and left.
The meeting was *hastily* arranged after the news broke.
She dressed *hastily* and ran for the bus.

senses.gloss: In a proud way that shows you think you are better than others.
examples: "I don't shop at discount stores," she said *haughtily*.
The waiter looked at us *haughtily* over his glasses.
He *haughtily* refused to answer.

position: mid — also before its word (*hazily defined*)

senses.gloss: Not clearly; in a vague or blurry way.
examples: I only *hazily* remember the night of the party.
The mountains were *hazily* visible through the smoke.
The goals of the program were *hazily* defined from the start.

form: compound of *head* + *on*; also an adjective (*a head-on collision*)

senses.gloss: With the fronts hitting each other directly.
examples: The two trucks collided *head-on* on the bridge.
The car hit the tree *head-on*.

senses.gloss: Directly, without trying to avoid a problem.
examples: The mayor decided to face the crisis *head-on*.
We need to tackle this issue *head-on*.

ru: в прямом противостоянии, один на один
form: compound; also an adjective (*a head-to-head race*)

senses.gloss: In direct competition, one against the other.
senses.ru: в прямом противостоянии, один на один
examples: The two phone makers compete *head-to-head* for the same buyers.
The candidates will go *head-to-head* in Tuesday's debate.
We tested the two vacuums *head-to-head*.

modifies: verbs of movement and of starting something

senses.gloss: With your head in front of the rest of your body.
examples: He dove *headfirst* into the pool.
The runner slid *headfirst* into second base.

senses.gloss: Quickly and eagerly, without stopping to think.
examples: She jumped *headfirst* into her new business.
Don't rush *headfirst* into a mortgage you can't afford.

form: compound of *head* + *-long*; also an adjective (*a headlong rush*)

senses.gloss: Very fast and without thinking or looking where you are going.
examples: The country is rushing *headlong* into war.
He ran *headlong* into the crowd.
They plunged *headlong* into a marriage after two weeks.

senses.gloss: With the head in front.
examples: She tripped and fell *headlong* down the stairs.
The boy dove *headlong* into the snow.

contrast: In everyday American speech *eat healthy* is far more common than *eat healthily*; careful writing prefers the *-ly* form.

senses.gloss: In a way that is good for your body or health.
examples: It's hard to eat *healthily* when you travel for work.
She's been living more *healthily* since she quit smoking.
The plants are growing *healthily* in the new soil.

position: end — mid before verbs like *agree* and *recommend*

senses.gloss: Loudly, warmly, or with great enjoyment.
examples: Everyone laughed *heartily* at his story.
After the hike, we ate *heartily*.
Our host shook my hand *heartily*.

senses.gloss: Completely; very much.
examples: I *heartily* agree with the committee's decision.
By Friday I was *heartily* sick of the whole project.

senses.gloss: Cruelly, without any sympathy or kindness.
examples: The landlord *heartlessly* evicted the family in December.
He dumped her *heartlessly* by text message.
The company treated its oldest workers *heartlessly*.

senses.gloss: In an angry, excited way, especially in an argument.
examples: The two senators argued *heatedly* on live TV.
Parents debated the new policy *heatedly* at the meeting.
He *heatedly* denied the accusation.

position: mid or end — before its word with participles (*heavily armed*)

senses.gloss: A lot; to a great degree or in a large amount.
examples: It rained *heavily* all night.
The city relies *heavily* on tourism.
He used to drink *heavily*.

senses.gloss: With a lot of weight or effort; slowly and noisily.
examples: She sat down *heavily* on the couch.
He was breathing *heavily* after climbing the stairs.

senses.gloss: Thickly or densely.
examples: It's one of the most *heavily* populated parts of the state.
The hills behind the town are *heavily* wooded.

senses.gloss: Without paying attention to danger or to what might happen.
examples: Drivers sped *heedlessly* past the stopped school bus.
He spent his savings *heedlessly* on cars and trips.
The boy ran *heedlessly* into the street after his ball.

senses.gloss: In a way that is useful or intended to help.
examples: A clerk *helpfully* pointed us to the right line.
The recipe *helpfully* lists the cooking times.
"The exit's behind you," he said *helpfully*.

senses.gloss: Without being able to do anything to help or control the situation.
examples: We watched *helplessly* as the house burned.
The baby cried *helplessly* in the crib.
She laughed *helplessly* until tears ran down her face.

form: rhyming compound; also an adjective (*a helter-skelter schedule*)

senses.gloss: In a confused, disorderly, hurried way.
examples: Papers were piled *helter-skelter* on his desk.
When the alarm went off, people ran *helter-skelter* for the exits.
Toys lay scattered *helter-skelter* across the living room.

type: time — formal; everyday English says *from now on*
position: front — also mid in formal writing

senses.gloss: From this time on.
examples: *Henceforth*, all visitors must sign in at the front desk.
The street will *henceforth* be known as Lincoln Avenue.
The company announced that it would *henceforth* use only recycled paper.

contrast: *The hereafter* (life after death) is a noun, not this adverb.

senses.gloss: In the rest of this document (used to introduce a short name).
examples: Johnson Construction, Inc. (*hereafter* "the Contractor") agrees to the following terms.
The University of Michigan, *hereafter* called "the University," owns the data.

senses.gloss: From now on; in the future.
examples: All payments will *hereafter* be made online.
Any student caught cheating will *hereafter* be expelled.

type: manner — formal, in official statements and legal texts

senses.gloss: By means of this statement or document.
examples: I *hereby* resign from my position as treasurer.
This meeting is *hereby* called to order.
You are *hereby* notified that your lease will end on June 30.

position: after its word — after a participle (*contained herein*); front in *Herein lies*

senses.gloss: In this document, statement, or situation.
senses.ru: здесь, в этом документе, в этом
examples: The information contained *herein* is confidential.
All terms described *herein* apply to both parties.
The two teams want different things, and *herein* lies the problem.

position: mid — also before its word (*heretofore unknown*)

senses.gloss: Until now; before this time.
examples: The letters reveal a *heretofore* unknown side of the president.
The court had *heretofore* rejected such claims.
The study found a *heretofore* unnoticed link between the two diseases.

position: before its word — almost always in *hermetically sealed*

senses.gloss: So tightly closed that no air can get in or out.
examples: The food comes in *hermetically* sealed packages.
The samples were stored in *hermetically* sealed jars.
He lives in a *hermetically* sealed world of rich friends.

senses.gloss: Very bravely, or with great effort against difficulty.
examples: The crew fought *heroically* to save the ship.
She *heroically* pulled two children from the river.
The nurses worked *heroically* through the pandemic.

senses.gloss: Slowly and uncertainly, because you are nervous or unsure.
examples: The new student raised her hand *hesitantly*.
He *hesitantly* knocked on the door.
"I think so," she said *hesitantly*.

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle; end after a verb

senses.gloss: In a very ugly or horrible way.
examples: The victim's face was *hideously* scarred.
The old mall was *hideously* remodeled in the 1980s.

senses.gloss: Extremely, in an unpleasant way.
examples: Rents in this city are *hideously* expensive.
The meeting was *hideously* long.

position: before its word — before a participle (*hierarchically organized*); end after a verb

senses.gloss: In levels or ranks, from the most important to the least.
examples: The army is a *hierarchically* organized institution.
Files on the computer are arranged *hierarchically* in folders.
Older companies tend to be run more *hierarchically* than startups.

position: before its word — before an adjective; end after a verb

senses.gloss: In an extremely funny way.
examples: The movie is *hilariously* bad.
She described her first date *hilariously*.
The furniture instructions were *hilariously* hard to follow.

position: mid — also before its word (*hitherto unknown*)

senses.gloss: Until now, or until the time being described.
senses.ru: до сих пор, до того времени, ранее
examples: Researchers found a *hitherto* unknown painting in the attic.
The rules, which had *hitherto* applied only to banks, now cover insurers.
The discovery answered a *hitherto* unsolved question.

senses.gloss: In a rough, low voice, as when your throat is sore.
examples: "Water," he whispered *hoarsely*.
After the concert, she could only speak *hoarsely*.
The fans cheered *hoarsely* in the final minutes.

position: end — also before a participle (*honorably discharged*)

senses.gloss: In an honest, fair, and respectable way.
examples: He served *honorably* in the Marines for twelve years.
She was *honorably* discharged in 2004.
Both sides behaved *honorably* during the negotiations.

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle; end after a verb

senses.gloss: Completely, in a way that cannot be fixed.
examples: We were *hopelessly* lost in the woods.
He's *hopelessly* in love with his neighbor.
The software is *hopelessly* out of date.

senses.gloss: Without any hope.
examples: She stared *hopelessly* at the pile of bills.
He shrugged *hopelessly* and walked away.

senses.gloss: Flat, or across from side to side, parallel to the ground.
examples: Fold the paper *horizontally*.
The stripes on the flag run *horizontally*.
Store wine bottles *horizontally* so the corks stay wet.

position: end — before its word with adjectives

senses.gloss: Very badly; in a terrible or shocking way.
examples: Everything went *horribly* wrong on opening night.
He was *horribly* injured in the explosion.
The team played *horribly* in the second half.

senses.gloss: Very; extremely (about something unpleasant).
examples: I felt *horribly* embarrassed.
Tickets were *horribly* expensive this year.

position: before its word — before an adjective; front as a comment on the whole sentence

senses.gloss: In a way that shocks and frightens; shockingly.
examples: The number of overdose deaths is *horrifyingly* high.
The crash scene in the movie is *horrifyingly* realistic.
*Horrifyingly*, the error went unnoticed for months.

form: the noun *horseback* used as an adverb
contrast: American English: *ride horseback*. Elsewhere, and with other verbs, say *on horseback* (*police on horseback*). *Horseback riding* is the American name for the activity; British English says *horse riding*.

senses.gloss: On a horse.
examples: We rode *horseback* along the beach at sunset.
My grandfather rode *horseback* to school in Montana.
Visitors can ride *horseback* through the canyon.

senses.gloss: In a friendly, generous way toward guests or visitors.
examples: The villagers treated us very *hospitably*.
We were *hospitably* received at the embassy.
Our host *hospitably* insisted that we stay for dinner.

position: before its word — before a participle (*hotly debated*); mid or end with verbs

senses.gloss: With strong feeling or intense effort, not about temperature.
examples: Gun control remains a *hotly* debated issue.
The senator *hotly* denied the report.
It was one of the most *hotly* contested elections in years.

senses.gloss: In an annoyed, offended way, often over something small.
examples: "Fine, do it yourself," she said *huffily*.
He *huffily* left the room when nobody laughed at his joke.
The customer walked out *huffily* without paying.
